title: Email Send-After-Hours Trend
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar exports (`calendar:event`), email metadata (`email:metadata`), password-audit reports (`passwordmanager:audit`).
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, password-audit exports, and calendar/email feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=email:metadata direction=outbound
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| where hour>=20 OR hour<7
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count as after_hours_sends by _time
| where after_hours_sends>10
| sort - after_hours_sends
description: Counts how many emails you send outside normal hours, a simple pulse on boundary creep and late-night cognitive residue.
value: A few nighttime messages are fine; a sustained trend often means work is spilling into time you wanted for recovery or family.
implementation: Forward email metadata with direction and timestamp; review weekly after-hours volume and decide whether the pattern is intentional.
visualization: Weekly line chart of outbound after-hours email count.
grandmaExplanation: It warns how much email you are sending late at night or very early, outside your normal day.
